chrome:
Mirror
Radial Planar Recursive Reveal

panels.name: hero
panels.html:
MIRROR

One photograph of one light well. Every shape after this is the same picture, reflected against itself.

panels.name: p1
panels.html:
Eight cells, not eight copies.

A block sliced by virtual mirrors. Every second cell is reversed, so each line meets the seam at the angle it arrived and the join disappears.

panels.name: p2
panels.html:
Straighten the mirrors.

The same operation, axis aligned instead of radial. Six bands, alternating reflections, sliding against each other.

panels.name: p3
panels.html:
Then put it inside itself.

Each copy scaled by the same ratio and turned by the same angle. The map preserves angles, which is why every repeat still reads as the same building.

panels.name: p4
panels.html:
Nine of it, offset.

Duplicated and slid out of register, then allowed to fall back into a grid it was never built for.

panels.name: p4b
panels.html:
Now tilt the mirrors.

Four planes at seventeen, fifty-eight, ninety-six and one hundred and forty-one degrees. Nothing lines up with anything, and the reflections still agree, because a mirror does not care about your grid.

panels.name: p5
panels.html:
And it was flat all along.

Turn the whole thing on its own axis and the depth goes with it. One picture. Nothing was ever added.
